Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment on procurement readiness and next steps: 

- Primary drivers: ramping automation across billing and reporting; looking to embed LLM-based summarization into finance ops workflows.
- Procurement constraints: central AP team requires vendor onboarding + W9; preferred payment is PO on Net 30 for vendors over $25k/year, but small purchases via corporate card are allowed with pre-approval.
- Marketplace interest: you mentioned potential procurement via your cloud marketplace to simplify vendor onboarding if pricing/terms align.

Questions / asks (from our side):
1) Can you confirm whether the initial pilot (estimated ~$12k for 3 months) will go through PO or card?
2) If PO is required, do you have a standard PO template and vendor onboarding packet we should complete (vendor form, W9, COI)?
3) Would using your cloud marketplace be preferred to avoid additional vendor paperwork, or is the marketplace only for production purchases?

Attached: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (Redwood standard) and an initial quote: redwood-quote-20270401.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
- Sophie: confirm AP path (PO vs card) and list of required paperwork by Tue 4/20.
- Lauren / Marissa: ready to expedite vendor packet and provide any additional commercial paperwork / SOC evidence.
- If PO required, we can provide an SOW + invoice and accept net-30 terms for the pilot.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 15-min call if useful.

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from AP side: 

- For a pilot at ~$12k we can pay via corporate card if Procurement signs off; however, our default is PO-Net30 for any vendor relationship expected to exceed $25k/year. Given this is a pilot with potential to expand, Procurement will likely push for a PO.
- Our vendor onboarding packet: we need a completed vendor form (you attached one — great), a W9, and evidence of SOC 2 Type II or equivalent. COI is optional for SaaS but good to have.
- Marketplace: our cloud marketplace (FinOps Marketplace) is preferred for speed if Redwood is listed and pricing matches the quote. It skips a lot of manual vendor onboarding. For pilots it can be used, but some internal groups still prefer a direct vendor relationship for contract flexibility.

Action items on our side:
- I will confirm by EOD Tue 4/20 whether Procurement will approve a one-off card payment for the pilot or require a PO.
- If they require a PO, I’ll attach the procurement checklist and the PO template for you to review.

Looping in Tom (vendor ops) for any specific onboarding questions.

Cheers,
Sophie Martin
Sr. Procurement Manager, FinOpsCo
